stories.summary:
Buffalo’s Power Play Coming Around as the PK Sinks Further



Score: Buffalo Sabres 5-3 Florida PanthersShots: BUF 32-23 FLA



Buffalo Sabres Goals: Doan 1st (Krebs) Dahlin 2nd PPG (Quinn, Thompson) McLeod 1st (Zellweger, Power) Ostlund 2nd PPG (Benson, Quinn) Thompson 4th (Power, Krebs)Florida Panthers Goals: Lundell 1st ( Ekblad, Vilmanis) Reinhart 1st PPG (Jones, M. Tkachuk) Reinhart 2nd PPG (B. Tkachuk,  Jones)



Plus 1: Sabres Pounce Early 



The Sabres came out with some jam today, firing shots early and generating better scoring chances than we’ve seen recently. Buffalo registered the game’s first five shots, keeping Jacob Markstrom busy right from the get-go. Josh Doan had one of the better opportunities, backhanding a rebound on goal from about 12 feet out. No dice for the snakebitten and apparently ailing Josh.



Buffalo cashed in at the 5:58 mark, with the aforementioned Josh Doan finally breaking his personal goose egg on the season. On a rush, Josh worked a give-and-go with Peyton Krebs, dishing him the puck near center ice. Krebs returned the favor with a perfect pass, sending Doan skating into the Panthers’ zone before he fired it past Markstrom. That was a King Kong-sized monkey finally coming off Doan’s back. The Sabres were dominating the early action, outshooting Florida 8-1 at that point.



A little later, Josh Norris had a golden opportunity when he redirected a pass off the wall toward the net while all alone in front. This time, Markstrom came up big. That missed chance would prove costly. Shortly afterward, Colton Ellis made the initial stop for Buffalo but couldn’t corral the rebound. After a scramble for the puck, Anton Lundell’s backhand somehow squeaked between Ellis’s pads—a weakness that has shown up a few times already—and into the net to tie the game.



Thankfully, Buffalo wasted little time getting that goal back on the power play. Steady now, folks—it’s true! Rasmus Dahlin unleashed a blast that found the back of the net, with Jack Quinn and Tage Thompson picking up the assists. However, credit Noah Ostlund for making it happen in the first place. His stickhandling and patience in the corner helped create the opportunity that led to the goal.



The Sabres earned another man advantage late in the period, but this one was nowhere near as effective. After 20 minutes, Buffalo held an 11-7 edge in shots and a 2-1 lead on the scoreboard. The Sabres were bringing the energy early and often and played a good period of hockey.







Minus 1: PK Struggles and the Captain Goes Down



Though it wasn’t a bad period for Jacob Markstrom, Florida head coach Paul Maurice decided to make a change, inserting Akira Schmid in goal to start the second. Perhaps he was looking to shake things up a little, and for the most part, it seemed to work.



Olen Zellweger, who had been skating well all afternoon, helped generate several good chances for himself and his teammates during a strong shift early in the period. Buffalo earned another power play shortly after when Aaron Ekblad was called for interference on Josh Doan. The Sabres generated some decent looks but, once again, came away empty-handed.



Zellweger then found himself in the penalty box for tripping Sam Reinhart, and the former Sabre wasted little time making Buffalo pay. Reinhart scored on the power play for his first goal of the year — just as many predicted in the pregame. Once again, the puck squeaked between Colton Ellis’s pads before being tapped into the net. At this point, head coach Lindy Ruff decided to join in on the goalie-change festivities, pulling Ellis after he surrendered two goals on just nine shots. Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen entered the game and was greeted by the boo birds from the KeyBank Center faithful. Buffalo has generally done a decent job of limiting opponents’ shots this season, but the goaltending simply hasn’t been there.



The Sabres responded with Ryan McLeod netting his first goal of the year. Toothless drove to the net, got around the defense, deked Schmid and tucked the puck home. Credit Owen Power and Zellweger for quickly transitioning the puck up ice and helping create the scoring opportunity. But the fans barely had time to settle back into their seats before gritty forward Beck Malenstyn, who had been having a solid shift, was whistled for holding. Former Sabre Sam Reinhart would strike again, burying his second power-play goal of the game. Buffalo’s penalty kill has been nearly as dreadful as it’s man advantage, and that’s saying something.



After two periods, the game was tied at three. However, the biggest concern had little to do with the scoreboard. Sabres captain Rasmus Dahlin was absent from the bench for some time before the team finally announced he had suffered an upper-body injury and would not return. Because apparently, this struggling team didn’t have enough problems already.



Plus 2: From Booooo to Luuuuuu



The third period opened cautiously, with both teams managing just one shot apiece through the first five minutes. Buffalo eventually put together a strong shift, capitalizing on a turnover behind the net and generating several chances around the Florida goal. The pressure paid off when Aaron Ekblad was called for holding Zach Benson, giving the Sabres a power play that would ultimately prove to be the difference in the game.



Buffalo’s man advantage showed some more life as Noah Ostlund scored his second goal of the season. Ostlund fended off a Panthers defender before swiping the puck past Schmid to give the Sabres some much-needed insurance. Benson deserved plenty of credit for the goal after a slick pass and some nifty stickhandling behind the net, while Jack Quinn picked up his second assist of the game.



Luukkonen then came up with a big stop on a Garnet Hathaway tip, along with several other tough saves after allowing a goal shortly after entering the game. Those saves proved crucial when Owen Power found Tage Thompson alone in the slot. TNT made no mistake, ripping a rocket past the Florida goaltender for his team-leading fourth goal of the season. Just like that, Buffalo had a two-goal cushion. Peyton Krebs also collected his second assist of the game on the play.



From there, the Sabres dug in and made Florida work for everything, with Luukkonen holding the fort behind them. UPL turned aside all nine shots he faced in the third period, delivering arguably his best performance in a single frame this season. That included surviving a late Florida power play with the Panthers pulling their goaltender for an extra attacker.



Buffalo bent but didn’t break, hanging on for a much-needed victory. The win stopped the bleeding and gave the Sabres a respectable 3-2 finish to their five-game homestand. After a frustrating stretch, these were two points Buffalo desperately needed.









Final Thoughts:



The Sabres needed this win in the worst way, and they delivered a strong effort overall. Buffalo overcame many of the same adversities that have plagued them through the first six games of the season. Tage Thompson, Jack Quinn and Peyton Krebs each finished with two points, while Josh Doan and Ryan McLeod finally scored their first goals of the season. I also thought Olen Zellweger had a terrific game, skating hard, moving quickly and making his presence felt all over the ice. Zach Benson stood out as well, bringing his usual energy and tenacity.



The loss of Rasmus Dahlin is a major blow, and as of now, there is no timetable for his return. Hopefully, Lindy Ruff will have some positive news to share soon. The Sabres can ill afford to be without their captain for an extended stretch.



Buffalo is right back at it tomorrow night when they visit the Montréal Canadiens at the Bell Centre. This will be the first meeting between the two teams since the Sabres fell to Montreal in Game 7 of the second round of last season’s playoffs. There should be no shortage of motivation for Buffalo in this one. Take note of the unusual 6:30 p.m. Eastern start time.
